examples.en: Sit on the floor. Then grab your toes.
I stubbed my toe on the desk.
My sneakers are small, so my toes hurt.
My toes are warm when I wear socks.
I put nail polish on my toenails.

examples.en: Press your palms together in front of your chest.
My palms get sweaty before an interview.
I wrote a note on my palm with a pen.

examples.en: My friend held out his palm. I gave him a high five too.
On cold days I rub my palms together.

phrases.en: (to change) as easily as turning over one's hand
phrases.nuance_en: used when someone changes their words or attitude very easily
phrases.en_equiv: (to change) as easily as turning over one's hand

examples.en: Press the soles of your feet together.
I walked a long way, so the soles of my feet hurt.
The soles of my feet were ticklish, so I laughed.
On a summer beach the soles of your feet get hot.
I got a blister on the sole of my foot.

phrases.nuance_en: used when you rush around very busily
phrases.en_equiv: to be run off one's feet, to rush around busily

phrases.en_equiv: to be too ashamed to face someone

examples.en: Keep your bottom on the floor.

phrases.nuance_en: used about someone who stays seated or in one place for a long time

I brush my teeth after a meal.
If you don't brush your teeth, they hurt.

explain: ‘양치질’은 이를 닦는 일을 말하는 명사예요. 동사로는 ‘양치질하다’보다 짧은 ‘양치하다’를 더 많이 써요. ‘이를 닦다’도 같은 뜻이에요.
explain_en: '양치질' is the noun for the act of brushing your teeth. As a verb, the shorter '양치하다' is more common than '양치질하다'. '이를 닦다' means the same thing.

examples.en: In the morning I have sliced bread and milk.
I spread jam on my bread.
I toast bread in the toaster.
We've run out of bread. I'll buy some at the supermarket.
I put cheese between two slices of bread.

dict_examples.en: Make a fried egg in oil, toast slices of bread, and put the egg between two pieces of toast.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
